statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays in the low band because the 29,116.75 session low has held for several hours and the range has not extended, while Stress remains elevated on live 50% US tariffs on about $28bn of Canadian goods, a 10-year yield close to a 20-month high and the 18:00Z Treasury press conference on Iran measures.
recommendation: Descriptive: NQ at 29,167.75 (-0.75%) at 11:14Z holds roughly 51 points above the 29,116.75 session low inside an unchanged 29,117-29,297 range, and the faded retracement from 29,232 is two-sided behaviour rather than the repeated extension after failed pullbacks that threatens a mean-reversion basket. ES -0.31% and YM -0.20% keep the weakness tech-specific, Treasury futures are bid with the 10-year at 4.72%, and WTI is 1.8% lower at $85.50 despite the Iran escalation, so no cross-asset amplifier is aligned. The narrow mapped danger window spans the 13:30Z US cash open through 14:30Z, with a secondary checkpoint at the 18:00Z press conference. Tail remains well below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100: session low holds into the US premarket as the retracement fades; Tail stays low, Stress elevated
body: NQ futures traded at 29,167.75, down 220.00 points or 0.75%, at 11:14Z against a 29,387.75 prior close, inside a 29,116.75-29,297.00 range that is unchanged from the previous assessment. The decisive observation for a mean-reversion basket is the shape rather than the direction: the retracement that reached 29,232 an hour earlier has faded back toward the lower part of the range, but the 29,116.75 low set in the early European hours is still untested after several hours and no new session extreme has printed. Two-sided rotation inside a fixed range is the opposite of the repeated extension after failed retracements that overwhelms the strategy, so the fade is scored as ordinary range behaviour rather than as the start of a trend leg, with acceptance below 29,116.75 the level that would change that read. Cross-asset confirmation stays absent. ES is 0.31% lower and YM 0.20% lower against NQ 0.79% lower on delayed contextual quotes, so the weakness remains tech-specific rather than a broad risk-off repricing, and European cash indices are steady. The live 10-year Treasury yield is 4.72%, marginally lower on the day after testing a 20-month high of 4.74% on Friday, the 2-year is 4.25%, and Treasury futures are bid from the 5-year through the long bond, so the curve is not the source of the equity pressure today even though the level itself keeps Stress elevated. The latest published H.15 constant maturities for 20 August were 4.19% at 2 years, 4.69% at 10 years and 5.23% at 30 years. WTI is 1.79% lower at $85.50 and Brent 1.26% lower at $93.20, a disinflationary offset rather than an amplifier, and notably no supply premium is priced ahead of the Treasury announcement on Iran; reporting attributes the decline to profit-taking after last week's rally and to a temporary rise in tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz. Gold is 0.48% higher. VIX is the one indicator that has firmed, at 16.03 and up 5.95%, sitting near the top of a narrow 15.86-16.05 intraday range but still close to the bottom of a 13.38-35.30 52-week range, which is a mild single amplifier rather than a regime shift. The index drag is concentrated in semiconductors, where the latest completed session left all seven tracked names lower with a mean decline near 1.8%, led by MU at 3.4% and ARM at 2.4% lower, while the megacap set closed dispersed with three of eight higher. Dispersion of that kind dilutes the aligned selling that a one-way index path requires. The macro backdrop supplies the elevated Stress rather than the Tail. US tariffs of 50% on roughly $28bn of Canadian goods took effect on 22 August after Canada suspended negotiations, with dollar-for-dollar retaliation announced for 8 September, and Treasury Secretary Bessent holds a press conference at 18:00Z detailing an expanded Iran sanctions campaign aimed at foreign banks, shippers and oil buyers. Both are recognised and publicly trailed catalysts rather than unresolved discontinuities. Today's only scheduled US release is the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30Z. The week's dominant catalysts remain Nvidia's report after the close on 26 August, preceded that morning by Core PCE, the second GDP estimate and durable goods, followed by the Jackson Hole symposium and the Fed Chair keynote on 28 August. Tail is therefore set at 13 in the low band, Stress at 50 in the elevated band, and the narrow mapped danger window is retained across the 13:30Z-14:30Z US cash open, where the opening auction supplies the first genuinely new price-path evidence of the session.

lookbackSummary: Over the prior 24 clock-hours the published Claude series stayed green with EA_ON throughout. Tail held at 4 across the 23 August US session while Stress climbed from 36 to 45, then stepped to 15 at 22:00Z as the Asian tech decline began and settled into a 7-12 band overnight. The Asian weakness peaked in the published series at 07:00Z with Tail 19 and Stress 58 on a trend-down mode, eased to 17 at 08:00Z, and turned to a mixed mode from 09:00Z as the retracement was observed, printing Tail 12 then 11 with Stress easing from 50 to 49. Two hours on 23 August, 11:00Z and 12:00Z, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour path holds Tail in the low band and the EA_ON mapping for every hour except the 13:00Z and 14:00Z US cash-open window, where conditional Tail steps to 20 and maps to WATCH across the 13:30Z-14:30Z danger window. Stress stays elevated through the US session and peaks at 60 during the 18:00Z Treasury press conference on Iran measures, which is scored as headline whipsaw rather than an assumed outcome. Conditional risk then decays through the US close on the assumption of orderly price discovery, troughs with Stress in the low 40s overnight, and drifts back up through Tuesday's Asian and European sessions as the 25 August US calendar and Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia report come into view. Confidence declines steadily with forecast distance because no live evidence extends beyond the current hour.
